topIssues.title: Kona init-chain interop activation gate is disabled when `interop_time` is `None`
topIssues.author: digorithm
topIssues.body:
## Summary

In `MessageGraph::check_single_dependency`, the initiating-chain timestamp gate uses `unwrap_or_default()` on `interop_time`. When the initiating chain's `interop_time` is `None`, the gate degrades to `initiating_timestamp < 0 + block_time`, which is false for any real timestamp, so arbitrary logs on that chain are accepted as valid initiating messages.

## Location

`crates/protocol/interop/src/graph.rs:393-400`

```rust
} else if initiating_timestamp <
    rollup_config.hardforks.interop_time.unwrap_or_default() + rollup_config.block_time
{
    return Err(MessageGraphError::InitiatedTooEarly { ... });
}
```

The executing-chain check at line 369 uses `is_interop_active`, which correctly returns `false` on `None`. The bug is on the init-chain path only.

## Impact

The activation gate is the only thing distinguishing "real init message emitted post-interop" from "arbitrary log matching the layout." After it, kona only verifies the log exists at the claimed position with the claimed origin and payload hash (`graph.rs:414-466`). Pre-interop, those logs have no interop semantics — any contract can emit any payload.

With the gate disabled, any log on a chain whose rollup config has `interop_time = None` becomes a forgeable initiating message.

### Attack (single-prover deployment)

1. Chain B is in the dep set; its rollup config (bundled, oracle-supplied, or stale) has `interop_time = None` in kona's view.
2. Attacker emits — or finds — any log on chain B whose `(emitter, payload)` matches what a target contract on chain A trusts as a cross-chain message.
3. Attacker submits an executing message on chain A referencing that log.
4. Kona's fault proof: log exists ✓, origin matches ✓, payload hash matches ✓, header timestamp matches ✓, init-gate `ts < 0 + block_time` is false ✓ → **VALID**.
5. `L2toL2CrossDomainMessenger` on chain A delivers the call. Targets that authenticate by `(sourceChain, xDomainSender)` are spoofable.

The dispute game consults only the canonical prover. If kona accepts it, the state finalizes.

## Fix

Replace `unwrap_or_default()` with explicit `None`-rejection mirroring `is_interop_active` semantics: reject the message when the initiating chain has no `interop_time` configured, rather than treating it as `0`.

topIssues.title: Enable eatmydata in CI by baking it into ci-base-clang
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Summary

CI runners write a lot of devnet/Geth/reth state that gets thrown away as soon as the job finishes, but every `fsync`/`fdatasync`/`msync` still blocks waiting for the kernel to flush. Preloading `libeatmydata.so` turns those calls into no-ops. We've already seen this matter on `op-acceptance-tests` with op-reth commit times blowing out to 60-125s. #20785 tests out applying this change by installing via apt for just the acceptance-test job. Rolling it out as the default image gives every Go, contracts, and Rust job the same speedup with no per-job opt-in.

The plan is to add `eatmydata` to `ops/docker/ci-base-clang` and write its library path into `/etc/ld.so.preload` so it's always active. We already use `ci-base-clang` for the Rust jobs; ethereum-optimism/optimism#20786 (draft) is a prerequisite experiment that switches `default_docker_image` to `ci-base-clang` so the eatmydata change benefits every job from one place. We only persist caches on success, so the durability trade-off is irrelevant. ci-base-clang is just the chime/base:2026.03 image we use for most jobs with clang installed so should be compatible and is still keeping most things installed via mise and flexible.

We _may_ see run times reduce because of this, but primarily its about stability. Things can get so backed up that even relatively long timeouts are being exceeded and errors start cascading. Hopefully removing the disk pressure will solve that.

## Plan

### Step 1 — Confirm ci-base-clang is safe as the default image
- Land ethereum-optimism/optimism#20786 (this PR switches `default_docker_image` to the pinned `ci-base-clang` digest, no other changes). Compare run times vs develop; only proceed if there's no significant regression.

### Step 2 — Bake eatmydata into ci-base-clang (image PR)
File to change: ``ops/docker/ci-base-clang/Dockerfile``

Add `eatmydata` to the apt install list and write `/etc/ld.so.preload`. The install and preload must be in the same `RUN` (and the preload step must come after the install, otherwise the file references a library that doesn't exist yet):

```dockerfile
RUN apt-get update \\
 && apt-get upgrade -y \\
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \\
      clang llvm-dev libclang-dev \\
      eatmydata \\
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \\
 && echo \"/usr/lib/\$(uname -m)-linux-gnu/libeatmydata.so\" > /etc/ld.so.preload
```

`\$(uname -m)` handles amd64 + arm64 builds. The existing `USER root` / `USER circleci` framing is unchanged. The existing build wiring (``docker-bake.hcl`` target ``ci-base-clang``, ``.github/images.json`` entry pointing at ``ops/docker/ci-base-clang/**``) auto-rebuilds the image on this path change — no other workflow edits needed.

### Step 3 — Wait for the develop attestation
After step 2 merges, the develop build re-publishes the image with a provenance attestation against ``refs/heads/develop`` (signed by ``ethereum-optimism/factory``). The `security` workflow (``.github/workflows/security.yml``) only accepts attestations on that ref, so a PR build's attestation is not sufficient.

Grab the published digest from the GitHub Actions run logs or via:

```sh
gcloud artifacts docker images describe \\
  us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/ci-base-clang:<develop-sha> \\
  --format='value(image_summary.digest)'
```

### Step 4 — Bump the pinned digest (config PR)
Update the `sha256:…` reference in **all** of:
- ``.circleci/config.yml`` — both `default_docker_image` and `rust_base_image`
- ``.circleci/continue/main.yml`` — `c-default_docker_image`, `c-rust_base_image`, plus the passthrough defaults
- ``.circleci/continue/rust-ci.yml`` — same four locations
- ``.circleci/continue/rust-e2e.yml`` — same four locations
- ``.circleci/continue/docs-ci.yml`` — `c-default_docker_image` and `default_docker_image`

The `security` workflow runs on `.circleci/config.yml` changes and runs ``gh attestation verify`` against the new digest. If step 3's develop build hasn't completed, this PR will fail the security check.

### Step 5 — Sanity-check
- [ ] Spot-check job logs: `eatmydata --version` or `cat /etc/ld.so.preload` in a representative job
- [ ] Compare `op-acceptance-tests` and a heavy contracts job against pre-change run times
- [ ] Close ethereum-optimism/optimism#20785 (job-level eatmydata) once the image-level rollout lands — they're alternatives, not stacking

### Rollback
Revert the digest bump PR (step 4). The previous digest still has a valid develop attestation, so the security gate passes immediately.

## Notes / risks
- Setuid binaries (``sudo`` etc.) ignore ``LD_PRELOAD``/``ld.so.preload`` by glibc design — fine for CI.

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth/proofs): backfill the proofs window backward
topPRs.author: dhyaniarun1993
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds the ability to extend an OP proofs storage window backward — taking a node that's been running with a recent earliest and rewriting older historical records so the window covers earlier blocks. This is the foundational implementation; the merge-walk-based compute is correct but per-block cost scales with proof-window depth. Optimizations will follow in separate PRs.

Three pieces:
- API trait OpProofsBackfillProvider — a prepend-style writer surface alongside the existing OpProofsProviderRw. Mirrors prune in reverse.
- V2 MDBX implementation(MdbxProofsProviderV2) — prepend_block(block_ref, diff) writes the four V2 changeset tables and front-inserts into the four history-bitmap tables, then moves earliest to the parent.
- BackfillJob — the driver. Iterates from current earliest down to target_earliest_block, computing each block's diff and calling prepend_block. Per-step state-root validation against the reth header.

**Tests**

- [x] Full crate suite (269 tests) passes locally.
- [x] V2 backend tests (db/store_v2/tests.rs) cover `prepend_block` tests
- [x] BackfillJob integration tests (backfill/tests.rs)
 
**Additional context**

NA

**Metadata**

Closes #20790

topPRs.title: feat(op-supernode,op-interop-filter): raft-wal-backed LogsDB
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Replaces the op-supervisor `logs.DB` used by op-supernode and op-interop-filter with a new raft-wal-backed implementation that is fully atomic on every `SealBlock`.

Each sealed block is one raft-wal entry: a fixed-width 80-byte header (block hash, parent hash, timestamp, log count, execMsg count), then `logCount × 32`-byte log hashes, then `execMsgCount × 88`-byte executing-message records. `Contains` is therefore an O(1) memcpy into the hash array regardless of how many logs the block carries. `AddLog` buffers in memory; the next `SealBlock` writes the full entry in a single fsync'd raft-wal append.

`op-supervisor` is not touched — both call sites swap from `logs.NewFromFile` to `raftwallogdb.Open` (directory-rooted instead of a single file).

## Benchmarks against the existing logs.DB

One week of 1-second blocks (604,800 blocks), 8 logs/block, fsync per `SealBlock`:

| Backend | Write time | Per block | Disk |
|---|---|---|---|
| existing logs.DB (no fsync) | ~30 s | ~17 µs | 317 MiB |
| raft-wal + fsync | 7 m 46 s | 770 µs | 384 MiB |

At 197 logs/block (op-mainnet average), measured directly:

| Metric | raft-wal value |
|---|---|
| Write time (week) | 12 m 18 s |
| Per sealed block | 1.22 ms |
| Disk (week) | 3.75 GiB |

Read latency at 2,000 blocks / 8 logs:

| Op | logs.DB | raft-wal |
|---|---|---|
| `Contains` | 46 µs | 3.9 µs |
| `OpenBlock` | 47 µs | 3.0 µs |

The offset-index entry layout means `Contains` does not degrade with logs/block — a block of 2,214 logs still answers `Contains` with a single bounded read + memcpy + checksum.
